definition: PlateSpin Protect replicates server workloads and supports their recovery after service disruption.
example: A team tests failover for a protected workload in a recovery environment.

definition: Play therapy uses play within a therapeutic relationship to help children express experiences and develop coping skills.
example: A trained therapist observes themes as a child uses figures to tell a story.

definition: PLINK is a command-line toolset for managing genotype data and running population genetics or association analyses.
example: An analyst checks missing genotype calls before comparing cohorts.
sense_note: The uppercase label suggests the genetics tool; distinguish PuTTY's Plink.

definition: Plumbing drawing documents pipe routes, fixtures and connections for plumbing systems.
example: A drafter marks fixtures and drainage routes on a floor plan.

definition: Plumbing plans examination reviews plumbing drawings and supporting documents against applicable requirements for approval.
example: An examiner requests a missing drainage layout detail.

definition: Point-to-Point Tunneling Protocol tunnels PPP traffic over an IP network and was historically used for virtual private networks.
example: An administrator identifies it in legacy remote-access documentation.
sense_note: Identifying this legacy protocol is not an endorsement for new deployments.

definition: A police baton is a handheld impact weapon issued in some law-enforcement settings under agency policy and legal controls.
Policy analysis evaluates policy options, effects and tradeoffs to inform decisions.
example: An analyst compares the distributional effects of two transit funding proposals.

definition: Policy research and analysis gathers evidence about a public or institutional issue and evaluates how it informs policy choices.
example: A researcher synthesizes evaluations to compare alternative housing policies.

definition: Poll Everywhere collects and displays audience responses during presentations or events.
example: An instructor displays anonymous responses to a concept check.

definition: Polycom refers to a product family for business voice and video communication.
example: A company equips a conference room with an audio and video device.
sense_note: Could also name the company or a particular model.

definition: Positive airway pressure uses pressurized airflow to help maintain an open airway or support breathing.
example: A clinician checks whether a patient can comfortably use a prescribed device.

definition: POSIX is a family of standards specifying portable operating-system interfaces, including APIs and shell utilities for Unix-like environments.
example: A developer uses a standardized interface to build software for multiple compatible operating systems.

definition: Post Office Protocol retrieves email from a server and is commonly used in its POP3 version.
example: An email client downloads messages from a configured POP3 mailbox.

definition: PostCSS lets JavaScript plugins analyze or transform CSS.
example: A build uses a plugin to add selected browser prefixes before publishing stylesheets.

definition: PostgreSQL is an open-source relational database system supporting SQL, transactions and extensible data features.
example: A service stores orders and queries them using joins and aggregates.

definition: Postman designs, sends, documents and tests API requests.
example: A developer checks a response body and status code from an internal test endpoint.

definition: Postorder traversal visits a node's children before the node itself, conventionally visiting left before right for a binary tree.
example: A program calculates a directory's total size after calculating the sizes of its subdirectories.

definition: PouchDB is a JavaScript database library for storing documents locally and synchronizing with compatible remote services.
example: A form saves entries offline and synchronizes them when connectivity returns.

definition: Power Automate is a Microsoft tool for automating tasks and workflows across applications and services.
example: A workflow requests manager approval whenever a form is submitted.

definition: A power flow study calculates operating conditions in an electrical network under specified load and generation assumptions.
example: An engineer checks line loading and bus voltages for a proposed expansion.

definition: Power tool operation uses electrically, pneumatically or otherwise powered tools to perform work under appropriate controls.
example: A trained worker uses a powered drill to prepare holes for a fixture.

definition: Powered industrial truck operation controls forklifts and similar workplace equipment for moving materials within safe operating limits.
example: A trained operator moves a palletized load to an approved storage location.

definition: PowerSchool provides software for managing student information and other school administration processes.
example: A school office records student enrollment and checks attendance.

definition: Pre-sales engineering uses technical expertise to determine whether a proposed solution meets a prospective customer's requirements.
example: An engineer builds a proof of concept for a requested integration.

definition: Predictive analytics software builds, evaluates or applies statistical and machine learning models to forecast outcomes from data.
example: An analyst uses software to estimate demand from past sales.

definition: Predictive modelling fits a model to estimate unknown outcomes using available inputs.
example: A team predicts delivery times from past orders and evaluates errors on new data.

definition: Presentation design organizes a message into clear visual material suited to its audience and setting.
example: A designer replaces a dense slide with a labeled chart and an explanatory sentence.

definition: Presentation software creates and delivers structured visual presentations, typically as sequences of slides.
example: A trainer prepares slides with diagrams and presenter notes.

definition: PrestoDB is a distributed SQL query engine for running analytical queries across data sources without requiring the engine to own the storage.
example: An analyst uses connected sources to combine data-lake events with information from a database.

definition: Preventive dental care reduces the risk or progression of oral disease through routine care, monitoring and education.
example: A dental team provides preventive services and teaches the patient how to improve daily oral hygiene.

definition: Prezi is presentation software that can arrange content on a visual canvas and navigate between areas through animated transitions.
example: A presenter zooms from a project overview into each workstream.

definition: Price negotiation seeks an agreed price and related terms through discussion of value, constraints and alternatives.
example: A buyer offers a larger order in exchange for a volume discount.

definition: PrimeRx is pharmacy management software supporting prescription processing, inventory and dispensing workflows.
example: A pharmacy records prescription status and monitors related inventory.

definition: PRINCE2 is a structured project management method organizing governance, roles and work around controlled stages and business justification.
example: A project board reviews the business case and next-stage plan before authorizing further work.

definition: The Principles for Responsible Banking provide a framework for aligning banking strategy and practice with sustainable development and tracking impacts.
example: A participating bank assesses its major impacts and sets targets for areas it can influence.

definition: Print design prepares visual material for physical printing with attention to layout, typography, color and production constraints.
example: A designer sets the bleed on a brochure to meet the printer's specifications.

definition: Printed circuit board design arranges components and conductive traces while meeting electrical, mechanical and manufacturing requirements.
example: An engineer checks that connectors and traces fit a sensor board and its enclosure.

definition: A privacy impact assessment identifies how an activity handles personal information, evaluates risks and documents safeguards.
example: A team checks whether a service form collects more information than needed.

definition: Privileged access management controls, monitors and limits the use of accounts or credentials with elevated permissions.
example: An administrator receives approved temporary access that expires after a maintenance window.
